## 1. Claims match the current source tree

Fail. Lifecycle, claim/lease behavior, storage guarantees, configuration, and dependency direction drift in F1–F11.

The prior findings were substantially addressed, but residual and newly reached defects remain.

## 2. Adopter surface vs repo-local configuration

Pass. Repo-local configuration shown in the reviewed surface is appropriately framed.

## 3. Current behavior only

Pass. Legacy-marker matches are illustrative or generic rather than product-history claims.

## 4. No rotting counts

Fail. No volatile totals remain, but the hand-maintained Event-tag enumeration violates the same single-source requirement (F12).

## 5. Links and referenced paths

Pass. Full-scope link/anchor and addressable-item resolution checks pass.

## 6. Content standards

Fail. One relationship diagram is non-Mermaid arrow art (F13).

## Findings

1. **F1 — Lifecycle diagram gives the wrong initial state.** [README.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/README.md:100) starts every issue in `backlog`, but dependency-free `jit issue create` issues are persisted as `ready`. Remediate the diagram to show the actual creation state and present `backlog` as the blocked state.

2. **F2 — Lease acquisition’s assignment side effect is omitted and contradicted.** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:1076) says `jit issue claim` records the assignee after `jit claim acquire`; acquisition already assigns the issue. Remediate to say `issue claim` is only needed afterward to promote ready work to `in_progress`.

3. **F3 — Ordinary issue claiming is falsely called atomic coordination.** [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:308) labels `jit issue claim` “atomic,” although candidate selection and assignment are separate operations. Remediate to describe it as lifecycle assignment and direct exclusive coordination to `jit claim acquire`.

4. **F4 — Lease reference overstates advisory leases as preventing edits.** [claim.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/claim.md:10) says leases prevent conflicting edits, but they only prevent duplicate lease acquisition; writes remain possible without a lease when enforcement is off. Remediate with the advisory/enforcement distinction.

5. **F5 — Atomic-write guarantee includes append-only event writes.** [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:62) says all file writes are all-or-nothing replacements. `events.jsonl` is lock-serialized append I/O, not temp-file-and-rename replacement. Remediate the guarantee to distinguish atomic replacement writes from locked append logs.

6. **F6 — Expired leases are falsely said to appear in `query available`.** [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:460) claims expiry makes an issue available to that query. Lease acquisition assigns the issue, while `query available` requires it to be unassigned. Remediate to distinguish lease availability from queue availability and prescribe release/unassign when appropriate.

7. **F7 — Gitless operation is said to disable all document features.** [guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:536) contradicts filesystem-backed document archive and current-content operations. Remediate to limit the Git requirement to commit-pinned/history operations.

8. **F8 — Multi-agent configuration presents inert controls as operational.** [multi-agent-coordination.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/multi-agent-coordination.md:204) presents `worktree.mode`, TTL, heartbeat, and staleness settings as active coordination controls, although only lease enforcement and indefinite-lease limits are consumed. Remediate to use `--ttl` and explicit heartbeats, and label the other fields as compatibility/display-only.

9. **F9 — Lock-timeout default is incorrect.** [deployment.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/deployment.md:147) lists `JIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` as `30`; storage defaults it to five seconds. Remediate the table to `5`.

10. **F10 — Dependency direction is reversed in the glossary.** [glossary.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/glossary.md:54) says `A → B` means A blocks B. `jit dep add A B` means A depends on B, so B blocks A. Remediate the blocks/blocked-by/transitive definitions.

11. **F11 — Storage layout invents per-agent heartbeat files.** [storage-format.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/storage-format.md:284) describes `heartbeat/<agent-id>.json` liveness records. Heartbeats update `claims.jsonl` and the claims index; no per-agent files are written. Remediate the layout and record description.

12. **F12 — Event tags are hand-copied volatile data.** [storage-format.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/storage-format.md:187) enumerates the current serialized Event variants despite identifying the Rust enum as authoritative. Remediate by replacing the list with the source citation or a derived projection.

13. **F13 — Source-precedence diagram is not Mermaid.** [multi-agent-coordination.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/multi-agent-coordination.md:175) uses a multi-line arrow-art flow in an untyped fence. Remediate it as a Mermaid diagram.

Total findings: 13
